34500-the-gold-brick.title: The Gold Brick.
34500-the-gold-brick.creator: Mrs. Ann S. Stephens.
34500-the-gold-brick.description: A book by Mrs. Ann S. Stephens.. A low coast, burdened in every foot of its soil with the luxuriant growth of a tropical climate; a large town, straggling and flat, swarming like a hive of bees with turbulent life. Lights flickering wildly from the windows and dancing with a fantastic and red glare up and down the streets.

arxiv-2106-08033.title: Selecting a Match: Exploration vs Decision
arxiv-2106-08033.creator: Ishan Agarwal, Richard Cole, Yixin Tao
arxiv-2106-08033.description: Abstract In a dynamic matching market, such as a marriage or job market, how should agents balance accepting a proposed match with the cost of continuing their search? We consider this problem in a discrete setting, in which agents have cardinal values and finite lifetimes, and proposed matches are random. We seek to quantify how well the agents can do.

arxiv-2201-01012.title: Expected FU Ori Outburst Amplitudes from the Optical to the Mid-Infrared
arxiv-2201-01012.creator: Lynne A. Hillenbrand, Antonio C. Rodriguez
arxiv-2201-01012.description: Abstract Disks around young stellar objects (YSOs) consist of material that thermally emits the energy provided by a combination of passive heating from the central star, and active, viscous heating due to mass accretion. FU Ori stars are YSOs with substantially enhanced accretion rates in their inner disk regions.

arxiv-2210-10078.title: Anticaustics in a Fabry-Perot interferometer Journal: josaa
arxiv-2210-10078.creator: Luis L. Sánchez-Soto, Juan J. Monzón, Gerd Leuchs
arxiv-2210-10078.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Luis L. Sánchez-Soto, Juan J. Monzón, Gerd Leuchs. We address the response of a Fabry-Perot interferometer to a monochromatic point source. We calculate the anticaustics (that is, the virtual wavefronts of null path difference) resulting from the successive internal reflections occurring in the system.

arxiv-2210-17404.title: A DFT+U type functional derived to explicitly address the flat plane condition
arxiv-2210-17404.creator: Andrew Burgess 1, Edward Linscott 2, David D. O’Regan 1
arxiv-2210-17404.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Andrew Burgess 1, Edward Linscott 2, David D. O’Regan 1. A new DFT+ U U type corrective functional is derived from first principles to enforce the flat plane condition on localized subspaces, thus dispensing with the need for an ad hoc derivation from the Hubbard model.

arxiv-2307-01374.title: On Restricted Intersections and the Sunflower Problem
arxiv-2307-01374.creator: Jeremy Chizewer
arxiv-2307-01374.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Jeremy Chizewer. A sunflower with r r petals is a collection of r r sets over a ground set X X such that every element in X X is in no set, every set, or exactly one set. Erdős and Rado [ 5 ] showed that a family of sets of size n n contains a sunflower if there are more than n ! ​ ( r − 1 ) n n!(r-1)^{n} sets in the family.

arxiv-2311-04721.title: Mechanical strain induced topological phase changes of few layer ZrTe 5
arxiv-2311-04721.creator: Zoltán Tajkov, Konrád Kandrai, Dániel Nagy, Levente Tapasztó, János Koltai, Péter Nemes-Incze
arxiv-2311-04721.description: Abstract Understanding the topological aspects of the band structure of solids has fundamentally changed our appreciation of their properties. The layered, van der Waals transition-metal pentatelluride ZrTe 5 has proven on numerous occasions to be an excellent candidate for the study of controllable topological phase transitions.

arxiv-2311-18108.title: Behavior-based dependency networks between places shape urban economic resilience
arxiv-2311-18108.creator: Takahiro Yabe Institute for Data, Systems, and SocietyMassachusetts Institute of TechnologyCambridge, MA 02139 tyabe@mit.edu Bernardo García Bulle Bueno Institute for Data, Systems, and SocietyMassachusetts Institute of TechnologyCambridge, MA 02139 bernard0@mit.edu Morgan R. Frank Department of Inf
arxiv-2311-18108.description: Abstract Urban economic resilience is intricately linked to how disruptions caused by pandemics, disasters, and technological shifts ripple through businesses and urban amenities. Disruptions, such as closures of non-essential businesses during the COVID-19 pandemic, not only affect those places directly but also influence how people live and move, spreading the impact on other businesses and increasing the overall economic shock.

arxiv-2402-07464.title: Two-point closed string amplitudes in the BRST formalism
arxiv-2402-07464.creator: Isao Kishimoto, Shigenori Seki, Tomohiko Takahashi
arxiv-2402-07464.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Isao Kishimoto, Shigenori Seki, Tomohiko Takahashi. Two-point tree-level amplitudes in bosonic closed string theory are described by a correlation function within the BRST formalism, which respects manifest Lorentz and conformal invariance. In the derivation of the two-point amplitudes, we use the mostly BRST exact operator, which has been introduced for two-point open string amplitudes, and a closed string vertex with ghost number three, which has been explored in our recent work, in addition to the conventional one.

arxiv-2501-15663.title: On-demand storage and retrieval of single photons from a semiconductor quantum dot in a room-temperature atomic vapor memory
arxiv-2501-15663.creator: Benjamin Maaß, Avijit Barua, Norman Vincenz Ewald, Elizabeth Robertson, Kartik Gaur, Suk In Park, Sven Rodt, Jin-Dong Song, Stephan Reitzenstein, Janik Wolters
arxiv-2501-15663.description: Abstract Interfacing light from solid-state single-photon sources with scalable and robust room-temperature quantum memories has been a long-standing challenge in photonic quantum information technologies due to inherent noise processes and time-scale mismatches between the operating conditions of solid-state and atomic systems.

arxiv-2507-07349.title: Stratification-based Instrumental Variable Analysis Framework for Nonlinear Effect Analysis
arxiv-2507-07349.creator: Haodong Tian, Ashish Patel, Stephen Burgess Center for Genomic Medicine, Massachusetts General Hospital Broad Institute of MIT, Harvard MRC Biostatistics Unit, University of Cambridge BHF Cardiovascular Epidemiology Unit, University of Cambridge
arxiv-2507-07349.description: Abstract Nonlinear causal effects are prevalent in many research scenarios involving continuous exposures, and instrumental variables (IVs) can be employed to investigate such effects, particularly in the presence of unmeasured confounders. However, common IV methods for nonlinear effect analysis, such as IV regression or the control-function method, have inherent limitations, leading to either low statistical power or potentially misleading conclusions.

pmc-10635858.creator: Seoyoung Park, Yun-Hee Lim, Byung Hoon Yoo
pmc-10635858.description: BackgroundCerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leakage may cause intracranial hypotension and postural headache. Secondary intracranial hypotension may result from an iatrogenic dural puncture or traumatic injury associated with pain procedures.CaseA 45-year-old male developed a headache 26 days after spinal pain procedure. pmc-10730685.title: Transformer encoder with multiscale deep learning for pain classification using physiological signals
pmc-10730685.creator: Zhenyuan Lu, Burcu Ozek, Sagar Kamarthi
pmc-10730685.description: Pain, a pervasive global health concern, affects a large segment of population worldwide. Accurate pain assessment remains a challenge due to the limitations of conventional self-report scales, which often yield inconsistent results and are susceptible to bias. Recognizing this gap, our study introduces PainAttnNet, a novel deep-learning model designed for precise pain intensity classification using physiological signals.

pmc-11586401.title: A simple method of fabrication hybrid electrodes for supercapacitors
